The core operator is the scaling transformation β = rb, linking model predictions to bookmaker odds. As r increases, the threshold for placing bets becomes more restrictive, reducing both the number of bets and the likelihood of overfitting to noise. This creates a trade-off between frequency and precision in betting strategy. The empirical validation via bootstrap confidence intervals reveals that while the model shows promise at r=1.2, high variability undermines certainty. The failure mode occurs when r exceeds critical thresholds, causing insufficient data points for stable inference. The dual nature of this system lies in its ability to optimize for either strictness or volume depending on r, yet both paths converge toward diminishing returns unless adjusted dynamically. In GSE, this manifests as a state transition from aggressive to conservative betting regimes. The mathematical duality reflects the tension between exploration (lower r) and exploitation (higher r), with optimal performance occurring near r ≈ 1.2 where expected absolute return turns positive.
